Bull.story: Grocery and retail reach restaurant-like frequency, ads and DashPass lift take rate, Deliveroo and Wolt scale: revenue about $42B (+19%/yr); gross margin 55% as grocery and DashMart absorb their fixed costs; opex falls to 35% of revenue, so operating margin reaches about 20%; buybacks offset stock pay; 28× GAAP EPS.

Base.story: Growth fades from about 20% to about 10% over five years (about $36B of revenue, +15%/yr); gross margin drifts up to 54% on ads and grocery mix; opex falls to 38.5% of revenue as the global platform is finished and Deliveroo is integrated, so operating margin reaches about 15%; buybacks offset half of stock pay; 24× GAAP EPS. The Instacart deal is assumed value-neutral at the $17B price.

Bear.story: Growth falls to about 10% a year (about $28B of revenue) as share is lost to Uber and Amazon and grocery needs continued price investment; DashMart and the Instacart integration keep gross margin near 51% and opex near 44%, so operating margin stalls near 7%; Instacart's price is not earned back; 18× GAAP EPS.
